pairs.subject: transactions-over-a-replicated-log
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:545 The queue executes SQL directly against SQLite WAL, and searches of the context and repository found no consensus, replicated_log, applied_index, or log_index, so the replicated-log precondition does not hold.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:1071 The queue fences stale workers by job attempt number; it does not capture an applied-log index alongside a transaction snapshot.
crates/core/src/store_instrument.rs:610 The instrument measures a closure receiving a SQLite connection; it does not implement a transactional storage interface with its own transaction handles.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:1460 Job listing queries the pool directly, without a transaction write buffer, reconciled key list, or apply-time verification hash.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:587 The durable engine uses SQLite WAL directly, without a consensus library requesting state-machine snapshots.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:1452 The job read executes directly against the pool; there is no buffered transaction commit that could propose an empty replicated entry.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:1080 Completion uses an SQL status-and-attempt fence, rather than optimistic snapshot hashes checked when applying a replicated transaction.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:853 Claiming mutates the queue through one atomic SQL statement, without a consensus round trip or a verification-and-write log entry.
